## Exchanging a PAT for an Access Token

This uses the **OAuth2 client credentials grant**. Send the credentials in the **POST body** — never in the URL or query string.

### curl

```bash
curl -X POST "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials&client_id={client_id}&client_secret={client_secret}"
```

### Python (requests)

```python
import requests

tenant = "your-org"
response = requests.post(
    f"https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token",
    data={
        "grant_type": "client_credentials",
        "client_id": "your-client-id",
        "client_secret": "your-client-secret",
    },
)
response.raise_for_status()
access_token = response.json()["access_token"]
```

### Using the token

Pass the returned token as a bearer on every subsequent API call:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer {access_token}" \
     "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts"
```

> **Note:** `beta` endpoints additionally require the header `X-SailPoint-Experimental: true`.

### A few limits to know

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| PATs per user (max) | 10 |
| Rate limit | 100 requests / token / 10 s |
| 429 handling | Back off using the `Retry-After` header in the response |

---
